title: Short proof of the conditioning property for multi-dimensional Poisson point processes: the conditioning property (Theorem 2)
author: Nicolas Lanchier
work: Short proof of the conditioning property for multi-dimensional Poisson point processes
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the conditioning property for multi-dimensional Poisson point processes, printed as Theorem 2 of the paper (source0.tex lines 113--122; the environment carries the optional title Conditioning property and is unlabelled in the source), delivered together with the paper's own complete proof of it at source0.tex lines 123--157. The paper has exactly two theorem environments and only one of them carries a proof, so the counted unit is the paper's main and only proved result. The proof is complete and self-contained given the retained context. After setting a = lambda(A) and b = lambda(B), it computes P(U_i in A) = integral of phi over A = lambda(A)/lambda(B) = a/b and, using independence of the n uniform points, identifies the left-hand distribution with the binomial distribution Binomial(n, a/b) through the display numbered (1). It then evaluates P(card(A intersect {P_1,...,P_n}) = k given N(B) = n) by rewriting the event in terms of N(A), using the definition of conditional probability, splitting N(B) into the independent counts N(A) and N(B setminus A) (which is legitimate because A and B setminus A are disjoint, so axiom (A1') applies), and factorising the conditional probability into a product of two Poisson probabilities; substituting the Poisson mass function and the identity lambda(B setminus A) = b - a from axiom (A2'), it simplifies the expression to the binomial coefficient (n choose k) (a/b)^k (1-a/b)^(n-k), recovering Binomial(n, a/b) in the display numbered (2). The two sides are then equal term by term, which is the statement. The argument is short but it is not the textbook one-dimensional proof: the paper's point is precisely that the classical proof uses the independence and exponentiality of the gaps between consecutive occurrences, which has no meaning in R^d, so the whole content of the argument is the conditional computation above, and the author states in the introduction that no proof of the multi-dimensional statement could be found in the probability literature. Carrying it out requires knowing to split N(B) into N(A) and N(B setminus A), to justify independence from the axioms, and to recognise the resulting Poisson-to-binomial identity; no qualifying examination poses it in this generality, and the result is the paper's contribution. That places the unit in the upper qualifying-to-research range: H2.
